position.summary: South Korea entered the week under multiple simultaneous pressures. A DMZ mine blast attributed to North Korea triggered a sharp diplomatic confrontation, with Pyongyang rejecting Seoul's accusation and issuing a warning about boundary lines down to the millimeter, followed by a North Korean missile test. Ukraine's transfer of two North Korean soldiers without full prior notification to Seoul created a diplomatic row that President Lee Jae Myung was managing carefully. President Trump publicly touted a massive South Korean investment package in US energy projects including Alaska LNG, while Seoul insisted final decisions were still pending and that technical discussions were ongoing. President Lee confirmed that AI tools appeared to have been used in bank hacks, elevating the issue to a national technology-and-trust story. The Asian Games football gold medal was overshadowed by the team captain's comment on military service exemptions and the Song Min-ho suspended sentence. Record chip exports supported the economy, while a government website data leak was initially dismissed by some officials as fake news, backfiring in public trust. A disability care home scandal and prosecution reform debates added further domestic noise.
